usual_baseline: Most units miss the BSG two-week target. Timely cholecystectomy 6.6–32.6%, rising to 71% in one unit; inpatient Lap-C as low as 2%. Mean waits of 64 days to 11.2 weeks. Readmissions while waiting are common: 6 of 21 [2391], 32% [2774]. No documented reason for delay in 34.8% [2578].
fix_that_works: Structural change works. A consultant-led biliary service with live tracking and inpatient Lap-C: two-week Lap-C 27% to 69–79%, time to Lap-C 68 to 13 days [2342, 2422]. Expedited pathway and tracker: timely 15.2% to 43% [2774]. P2 listing and cancelling elective work: 71% to 86% [2745]. Re-audit 32.6% to 64.5% [2589].
fix_that_fails: COVID elective backlog took one unit from full compliance to 0 of 4 [2208]. Even after change, only half were operated [2774], and barriers persisted: ultrasound slots, hot lists and reluctance to operate acutely [2589]. Length of stay for index surgery rose from 3 to 6 days [2745].
consultant_advice: Heavily audited; every unit finds the same gap. Another baseline adds nothing. If you do it, audit the delay by step (fitness, MRCP, ERCP, theatre) and readmissions while waiting, and track whether a hot-list or tracker survives beyond a year.
